root_cause: In mv_npu_top/mv_postproc integration, completed row results are presented with pp_in_valid from hold_row_valid, but mv_postproc only consumes when (!bias_en || bias_valid). For bias_en=0, acceptance can still be blocked because in_ready depends on out_valid/out_ready; if out_valid is held and out_ready toggles low, hold_row_valid may remain asserted, which directly deasserts mat_ready (gated by !hold_row_valid), causing matrix ingress timeout. This control coupling also perturbs row handoff timing and leads to arithmetic mismatch in directed case.

evidence.observation: Assertion failure at 34ns: got [3, -52] vs expected [3, -55].
evidence.relevance: Earliest authoritative functional divergence before timeout symptoms.

evidence.observation: SimTimeoutError timeout waiting mat_ready during matrix send.
evidence.relevance: Confirms progress failure under runtime backpressure/handshake sequences.

evidence.observation: mat_ready is gated by !hold_row_valid; hold_row_valid is set on last chunk and cleared only when pp_in_ready.
evidence.relevance: Direct mechanism for ingress stall when postproc acceptance is delayed.

evidence.observation: Row consume/write requires in_valid && in_ready and conditional (!bias_en || bias_valid); in_ready depends on out_valid/out_ready.
evidence.relevance: Explains coupling of row acceptance to output backpressure and possible retention of hold_row_valid.

alternative_hypotheses: Latch warnings in mv_mac16_core combinational temporaries could cause value corruption, but current first causal control divergence is localized to top-level row/postproc handshake.
Width-truncation warnings may affect large-N addressing but do not explain immediate directed mismatch and mat_ready stall at small N.
